title: Objective interpretation of assent
summary: Words and conduct are read in their context as manifestations to the other party.
notes: Lucy protects a genuine and reasonable understanding despite a private joke. Keller involves shared knowledge of a joke, and Leonard concerns the reasonable meaning of an advertisement. Specht asks what a download communicates when notice is hidden. The opposing scholarly passages ask how far an objective account should exclude evidence of actual intention. A slogan that subjective intention never matters would erase important distinctions in this reading.
